incomeReassignment.sideEffect: the provision question disappears. Against blue at 221°, provision (emerald, 161°) sits 60° away instead of the 19° it had against green. Provision stays emerald and needs no move.

adjacencyFindingsRaisedByThisChange.finding: net is sky-600 (#0284c7, hue 200°). Income at blue-600 is 221°. That is 20.8° between the two figures that sit next to each other in every monthly summary.
adjacencyFindingsRaisedByThisChange.compounding: net is also only 11.7° from the brand cyan (189°) — the same defect Alfredo called on income. Sky is squeezed between the brand on one side and any blue we give income on the other. There is no rung of sky that fixes both.
adjacencyFindingsRaisedByThisChange.conclusion: net has to move off sky. This is not optional once income is blue.

optionA_recommended.proposal: net becomes neutral — fg/net = fg/default (slate-900), no hue of its own.
optionA_recommended.argument: net is the RESULT, not a component. Income, expense, tax and provision are the ingredients and each earns a hue; the total should read as the total. It also costs nothing — the value already exists — and it takes a hue out of an already crowded palette.
optionA_recommended.bonus: when net is negative it takes fg/expense (red). The sign carries the meaning instead of the hue, which is more honest than colouring a number blue whether it is good news or bad.

optionB.argument: keeps net as a distinct hue. 42° from income, 74° from the brand. Violet is entirely unclaimed.
optionB.cost: one more hue to hold in your head, on the number that matters most.

adjacencyFindingsRaisedByThisChange.resolution: net takes the brand cyan. See netDecision. Options A (neutral) and B (violet) are withdrawn.

adjacencyFindingsRaisedByThisChange.finding: bg/income (blue-600) is the same value as category/bank (blue-600).
adjacencyFindingsRaisedByThisChange.whyItIsProbablyFine: they occupy different visual roles — a category is a small glyph in a tinted chip, income is a figure or a bar. fg/income sits a rung darker at blue-700, so the two rarely render at the same value.
adjacencyFindingsRaisedByThisChange.ifItBothersYou: move category/bank to violet-600. Categories are arbitrary identity hues; the domain palette is not.

adjacencyFindingsRaisedByThisChange.finding: category/work is also sky-600 — the identical value to net today.

netDecision.proposedBy: Alfredo, 2026-08-20: 'depronto Net puede ser el mismo color de brand Neto, ya que la app se llama Neto y este valor al fin es neto'
netDecision.verdict: ACCEPTED — and it is stronger than either option I offered.
netDecision.theObjectionIHad: a hue cannot mean both 'this is tappable' and 'this is a number'. If cyan is the primary button AND the net figure, colour stops being a reliable affordance signal.

whyTheObjectionDied.finding: color/interactive/primary has exactly 18 TEXT bindings and every one of them is an onboarding eyebrow: 'PASO 1 DE 3' (4), 'PASO 2 DE 3' (8), 'PASO 3 DE 3' (6). Not one link, not one text button.
whyTheObjectionDied.conclusion: cyan text does not currently mean 'tappable' in this file. Nothing has to be given up for it to mean 'net'.

whereBgNetActuallyLives.measurement: color/net/default paints the DistribucionCard bar segment (125x16), the chart-legend dot (6x6), the KPI card swatch and two container bars.
whereBgNetActuallyLives.conclusion: bg/net is chart geometry, not a button-shaped surface. A cyan segment sitting next to income-blue, expense-red and tax-amber in the distribution bar does not read as a control — it reads as the total, which is exactly the intent.

implementation.why: Rule 7 — different job, different token, same value through an alias. Reusing fg/brand directly would weld 24 bindings together and make decoupling later a re-bind instead of a value change.

conditions.condition: the 18 eyebrow labels move off cyan to fg/subtle
conditions.why: once cyan means net, a cyan 'PASO 2 DE 3' is a false signal. This is the whole cost of the decision: eighteen bindings on three strings.

conditions.condition: fg/brand stops existing as a general-purpose token
conditions.why: after the eyebrows move, its only remaining job IS the net figure. Two names for one job is Rule 7 backwards. There is no fg/brand; there is fg/net.

this is what turns the idea from colour reuse into a real semantic. The sign carries the meaning, not the hue — and brand cyan then means 'estás en positivo', which is a good thing for a brand colour to mean in a planner.

sideEffects: sky-600 is freed. category/work stops being a duplicate of net.
the 11.7° net-to-brand collision does not get fixed, it gets dissolved: net is not NEAR the brand, it IS the brand. Nothing left to confuse.
income-blue (221°) sits 32° from the brand cyan (189°) and 60° from provision emerald. The whole domain palette separates cleanly for the first time.
